name: e2e-testing
description: The sole home for every browser-driven test in this marketplace, at any depth — a sibling frontend plugin's react-testing skill covers unit and integration only and hands off here for anything needing a real browser, whether a five-minute smoke check or a full cross-stack workflow. Drives a real frontend against a real backend and database with Playwright, verifying that a UI action produced the correct API request, business-logic result, and database state — not just a UI-visible success state. Sits between the frontend and backend plugins the same way api-contract does, but for runtime behavior instead of schema. Before designing any test, asks the user to choose testing depth (critical flows vs. comprehensive) and device/browser coverage as explicit multiple-choice options, then presents the full scenario list for confirmation before any code is written — human-in-the-loop at both the scoping and the implementation gate. Models frontend and backend as two distinct origins (a dual base-URL fixture, not one shared baseURL), brings both up locally via a webServer convention, and documents where the suite lives — inside the frontend repo, in a dedicated e2e/ folder, owning the @playwright/test dependency itself — plus a staging-only CI default with an explicit never-production warning. Includes test-case design/documentation, the page-object-model project structure, per-role auth-state reuse, a responsive/viewport matrix across mobile Chrome, mobile Safari, tablet, and desktop, and a Playwright best-practices review checklist. Optionally consults a sibling codebase-map plugin for cached, checkpointed codebase facts instead of re-scanning the repo every session.
